_meta.purpose: Seed reference set for the media-quiz fact-check (flaw 11) and the glossary used to protect terms during translation (flaw 13).
_meta.note: Small, hand-curated seed. Extend with entries from the NSSO manuals, the CPI handbook and the MoSPI glossary. A mismatch only FLAGS a question for trainer review; it never rejects it, so a stale entry costs a review, not a lost question.
_meta.fields: keywords: all must be non-empty; an entry matches when at least `min_hits` keywords appear in the question + correct answer. numbers: every value the reference accepts for this topic (old and revised series both count).

facts.statement: The CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) series compiled by NSO uses base year 2012=100; a revised series with base 2024 has been announced.
CPI in India is compiled with a (modified) Laspeyres base-weighted formula.
The current National Accounts series (GDP/GVA) uses base year 2011-12; a revision to 2022-23 has been announced.
The Index of Industrial Production uses base year 2011-12.
The Wholesale Price Index (compiled by DPIIT, not MoSPI) uses base year 2011-12.
facts.source: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT

facts.statement: India's national accounts follow the UN System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008); SNA 2025 is the newly adopted update.
The CSO and NSSO were merged into the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI in 2019.
The National Sample Survey was set up in 1950.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey was launched by NSO in 2017 (first annual report 2017-18).
In simple random sampling every unit (and every sample of the same size) has an equal probability of selection.
